name: Pinned Horizontal Scroll
description: Vertical scrolling is converted into a horizontal slide: the section pins to the viewport while a row of panels glides sideways, then releases. A portfolio/agency classic, without GSAP.
usage: Structure: .h-scroll > .h-sticky > .h-track > panels. Section height is set automatically from the track width so the pace feels 1:1.
tags: sticky, horizontal, gallery, pin, scrub, portfolio

name: Scroll Progress Indicator
description: A gradient bar fills across the top of the page as you read, bound directly to scroll position. Zero JS on modern browsers and runs off the main thread.
usage: Place .progress as the first child of body. The animation-timeline: scroll(root) binds it to the document scroll; use scroll(nearest) for a scroll container.
tags: css, animation-timeline, scroll(), progress bar, reading indicator

name: Scroll-Driven Reveal
description: Elements lift, scale and un-blur as they enter the viewport, driven purely by scroll position with CSS animation-timeline: view(). Scrubs forwards and backwards with the scrollbar.
usage: Add class "reveal" to any element. Tweak animation-range (entry 0% → cover 35%) to change when the animation starts and ends.
tags: css, animation-timeline, view(), fade, blur, no-js

name: Sticky Stacking Cards
description: Full-width cards pin one after another and pile up like a deck; each covered card scales down and dims, giving a satisfying sense of depth.
usage: Wrap cards in .stack and give each .stack-card a --i index. Top offset and scale step are CSS/JS variables (OFFSET, SCALE_STEP).
tags: sticky, stack, cards, depth, scale, features section

name: Text Fill on Scroll
description: A large statement paragraph starts dimmed; each word lights up in reading order as you scroll through it — the Apple / Linear storytelling look.
usage: Add data-scroll-fill to any text block. Words are split automatically. Tweak START/END (fractions of viewport height) to change when the fill starts and completes.
tags: words, opacity, scrub, storytelling, apple-style

name: 3D Tilt Card with Glare
description: A card rotates in 3D toward the pointer, inner layers float at different depths, and a glossy light glare slides across the surface — the premium "physical card" feel.
usage: Add data-tilt to a card. Children with data-depth="40" pop forward by that many px. MAX_TILT sets the angle.
tags: 3d, perspective, tilt, glare, holographic, card, parallax layers

name: Blend-Mode Cursor Follower
description: A soft circle trails the pointer with inertia and inverts whatever it passes over (mix-blend-mode: difference). It swells over links and buttons and shrinks on press.
usage: Include .cursor + script. Any element with data-cursor="grow" (or a / button) enlarges it. Change EASE for more/less lag.
tags: cursor, mix-blend-mode, difference, lerp, agency

name: Hover Image Reveal List
description: Hovering a project title in a big typographic list reveals a floating preview image that follows the cursor with inertia and tilts with velocity; other rows dim.
usage: Each .reveal-item gets data-color (or data-img for a real image URL). The preview element is shared.
tags: list, hover, preview, follow cursor, velocity, rotation, projects index

name: Image Trail
description: Moving the pointer leaves a trail of images that pop in, then shrink and fall away — a playful hero interaction seen on many award-winning portfolios.
usage: Put (or styled divs) inside .trail as the pool; they are recycled round-robin. GAP = distance in px between spawns.
tags: cursor, trail, images, web animations api, playful, portfolio hero

name: Magnetic Button
description: Buttons are pulled toward the cursor when it comes near, with the label drifting further than the shell for parallax; on leave they snap back with an elastic overshoot.
usage: Add data-magnetic to any element and wrap its label in .magnetic-label. Tune data-strength (0–1) and RADIUS.
tags: button, magnetic, cursor, elastic, cta

name: Spotlight Border Cards
description: A soft light follows the pointer across a grid of cards, illuminating their 1px borders and inner surface — neighbouring cards catch the edge of the glow. The signature Linear / Vercel feature-grid look.
usage: Wrap cards in .spotlight-grid; each .spot-card needs an inner .spot-inner. Glow colour and size are CSS variables on the grid.
tags: spotlight, border glow, radial-gradient, bento, linear-style, vercel-style

name: Infinite Marquee
description: Seamless endlessly looping rows of text or logos, in opposite directions, with faded edges and pause-on-hover. A tilted variant adds energy.
usage: Put items inside .marquee-track ONCE; the script duplicates them for a seamless loop. Set --duration and data-reverse per row.
tags: marquee, ticker, loop, logos, css only, edge fade, skew

name: Shimmer & Gradient Text
description: Two looks in one: a slow-flowing multicolour gradient headline, and a subtle light sweep that glints across muted text — the "AI is thinking" / premium badge shimmer.
usage: .text-gradient for flowing colour; .text-shimmer for the light sweep. Colours and speed are CSS variables.
tags: gradient text, shimmer, shine, background-clip, ai product, badge

name: Split Text Stagger Reveal
description: Headline letters rise out of an invisible mask one after another with a springy ease, line by line — the hero intro of countless award sites, without GSAP SplitText.
usage: Add data-split to a heading. Use data-split="words" to animate words instead of letters. Set --stagger on the element. Call replay(el) to re-run.
tags: split text, letters, mask, stagger, hero title, intro animation

name: Text Scramble / Decode
description: Text resolves out of random glyphs character by character, like a decoding terminal. Used for rotating headlines and on hover for nav links.
usage: new Scramble(el).setText('New text') returns a promise. Add data-scramble-hover to links to scramble their own label on hover. CHARS controls the glyph set.
tags: scramble, decode, glitch, hacker, monospace, hover, rotating headline

name: Variable Font Proximity
description: Each letter's weight swells smoothly as the cursor approaches, creating a living typographic wave that follows the pointer across the word.
usage: Add data-proximity to a heading set in a variable font. Configure MIN/MAX weight and RADIUS (px). Works with any axis via font-variation-settings.
deps: Google Fonts — Inter variable (any variable font works)
tags: variable font, font-weight, proximity, cursor, typography, wght axis

name: Aurora Mesh Gradient
description: Large blurred colour blobs drift slowly and blend into each other, producing a soft living mesh gradient behind a hero — pure CSS, cheap on GPU.
usage: Drop .aurora as the first child of a position:relative section. Change blob colours via --c1…--c4 and speed via --speed.
tags: gradient, mesh, blobs, blur, aurora, hero background, css only

name: Film Grain Overlay
description: A subtle animated film grain over the whole page that kills flat-gradient banding and adds tactile, analog warmth. Generated by an inline SVG turbulence filter — no image files.
usage:
Add
once at the end of body. Adjust --grain-opacity (0.05–0.15 is typical) and baseFrequency for coarser/finer noise.
tags: noise, grain, texture, svg filter, feTurbulence, analog, editorial

name: Interactive Dot Grid
description: A calm grid of dots that bulge away from the pointer and light up near it, then spring back with damped physics — a tactile, techy hero background.
usage: Place <canvas class="dot-grid"> behind content. Tweak SPACING, RADIUS, FORCE and colours at the top of the script.
tags: canvas, dots, grid, repel, spring physics, hero background, tech

name: Silk Turbulence Gradient
description: A soft, satin-like gradient whose colors fold into long silky ribbons and drift slowly, like light moving across fabric. Layered sine waves bend the coordinates and the result is mapped onto your own 2–5 color palette.
usage: <canvas class="silk" data-colors="#ff5c8f,#ff7aa6,#ffa3c4"> behind content, then new SilkGradient(canvas, { speed, scale, turbulence, frequency, iterations, waves, grain }). Change colors at any time with gradient.setColors(['#…', …]) or by editing data-colors. Close shades of one hue give the calm "satin" look; contrasting hues give a bolder flow.
tags: webgl, glsl, shader, turbulence, sine warp, silk, satin, gradient, hero, cta section, customizable palette

name: WebGL Flowing Shader Gradient
description: A full-bleed fragment shader paints a slowly flowing, silky gradient using domain-warped noise, subtly bending toward the pointer. Built-in grain prevents banding. The Stripe / "shader hero" look with zero libraries.
usage: Place <canvas class="shader-bg"> behind content. Edit the 4 palette vec3s in the shader and SPEED. Renders at reduced resolution (SCALE) for performance.
tags: webgl, glsl, shader, fbm, domain warping, stripe-style, fluid, hero

name: Circular Reveal Theme Toggle
description: Switching light/dark mode floods the new theme outward in an expanding circle from the exact point you clicked — a View Transition with a clip-path animation on the new snapshot.
usage: Call toggleTheme(event) from any button. Theme is driven by [data-theme] on <html>; swap in your own tokens.
tags: dark mode, theme toggle, view transitions, clip-path, circle wipe

name: Gooey Menu & Tabs
description: Interface pieces that melt into each other like liquid. A "+" button squeezes out menu items that drip away and pop free, and a tab indicator stretches like jelly between tabs. Labels and icons stay perfectly crisp.
usage: Two stacked layers with identical positions: a .goo-layer (solid shapes, filter: url(#goo-ui)) and a .crisp-layer (icons/text, no filter). Animate the shapes with CSS transitions; the filter does the merging. stdDeviation sets how far blobs reach for each other.
tags: gooey, svg filter, liquid ui, fab, floating action button, tabs, segmented control, jelly

name: Gooey Metaballs
description: A chain of blobs follows the cursor and melts together like liquid mercury when they touch, thanks to an SVG blur + alpha-contrast filter. Also great for gooey menus and buttons.
usage: Wrap shapes in a container with filter: url(#goo). Increase stdDeviation for softer merging; the matrix row "18 -7" sets edge sharpness.
tags: gooey, metaballs, svg filter, liquid, blob, cursor, merge

name: Liquid Glass
description: A draggable glass lens that refracts and warps the content beneath it, with specular rim highlights — the Apple "Liquid Glass" material for the web. Degrades to classic frosted glassmorphism.
usage: Put the <svg> filter once in the page, then add class .liquid-glass to any element. Strength = scale on feDisplacementMap; frost = blur().
tags: glassmorphism, liquid glass, refraction, svg displacement, backdrop-filter, apple 2025, draggable

name: Liquid Metal
description: Real-time liquid chrome flowing through button rings, icon buttons and badges. Reflections slowly ripple, a soft halo orbits the element and the metal bends toward the cursor as it approaches.
usage: Add class .metal to an element and give it a .metal-inner child for ring mode (the ring thickness is the inner inset, --ring). Add .metal-fill instead for a solid metal badge. One small WebGL canvas is created per element, so keep it to a handful per page.
tags: webgl, shader, chrome, liquid metal, mercury, button, ring, badge, cursor reactive

name: Rotating Conic Border Glow
description: A beam of light orbits the border of a card or button and casts a blurred glow behind it — animated with a registered @property angle so the conic-gradient rotates smoothly.
usage: Add .glow-border to an element. Change --beam colours and --speed. Works on any border-radius. Includes a rainbow "border beam" chat-input preset (see the .chat example).
tags: @property, conic-gradient, border, glow, border beam, ai, chat input, cta, card, houdini

name: Shared Element Morph (View Transitions)
description: Clicking a thumbnail morphs it seamlessly into a full detail view — position, size and radius interpolate natively via document.startViewTransition and view-transition-name. The same API powers cross-page (MPA) transitions.
usage: Give the element a unique view-transition-name in both states, then wrap your DOM update in document.startViewTransition(). For MPA sites add @view-transition { navigation: auto; }.
tags: view transitions api, shared element, morph, expand, gallery, page transition

name: Furry Bot Avatars
description: Plush, furry little characters for your AI agents. Their eyes wander and blink, they hop while working, and they doze off with closed eyes and floating z's when idle. Drawn on a plain canvas, no WebGL. Click one to make it jump.
usage: new BotAvatar(canvas, { shape: 'clover' | 'flower' | 'ghost' | 'square' | 'blob', color: '#3b82f6' }); avatar.setState('idle' | 'working' | 'sleeping'); avatar.jump(). The fur is rendered once to an offscreen canvas, so each frame is cheap.
tags: ai, agent, avatar, mascot, character, fur, canvas, squash and stretch, idle animation

name: Image Generation Loader
description: While an image is "generating", a churning mosaic of coloured pixels shimmers in place; when it's ready the mosaic sharpens through coarse-to-fine pixelation and dissolves cell by cell into the real picture.
usage: const fx = new ImageGenLoader(canvas, { palette }); then fx.reveal(imgOrUrl) once the image is ready; fx.reset() to start again. The canvas CSS size sets the output size.
tags: ai, image generation, loader, pixel mosaic, depixelate, dissolve, canvas, placeholder

name: Thinking Orbs
description: Tiny 3D particle orbs that signal an AI at work — a breathing dotted sphere, a rolling torus, a swirling galaxy and a listening wave — each paired with a shimmering status label.
usage: new ThinkingOrb(canvas, { variant: 'sphere' | 'torus' | 'galaxy' | 'listen', color: '#fff', speed: 1 }). Canvas CSS size sets the orb size (24–96px works best). Call orb.setVariant() to switch state, orb.destroy() to stop.
tags: ai, loading, thinking indicator, canvas, 3d dots, sphere, torus, particles, agent status

name: Voice Glow
description: A colourful aurora rises from the bottom of a chat input as you speak, its height and brightness following your voice level, then it sweeps side to side while the AI "thinks" about the reply.
usage: Wrap the input in .voice-wrap and add a .voice-glow sibling with 4 spans. Drive it with voice.setLevel(0–1) and voice.setState('idle' | 'listening' | 'thinking'), or call voice.useMic() to bind the real microphone.
tags: ai, voice, microphone, audio reactive, web audio, glow, chat input, siri-style
